code.heading: There are several ways to evaluate the performance of an ARIMA model. Here are some common methods:
code.code:
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error

# Calculate the mean absolute error (MAE)
mae = mean_absolute_error(y, model.predict_in_sample())
print('MAE:', mae)

# Calculate the mean squared error (MSE)
mse = mean_squared_error(y, model.predict_in_sample())
print('MSE:', mse)

# Calculate the root mean squared error (RMSE)
rmse = np.sqrt(mse)
print('RMSE:', rmse)

# Calculate the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE)
mape = np.mean(np.abs((y - model.predict_in_sample()) / y)) * 100
print('MAPE:', mape)

# Calculate the symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE)
smape = np.mean(2.0 * np.abs(model.predict_in_sample() - y) / (np.abs(y) + np.abs(model.predict_in_sample()))) * 100
print('SMAPE:', smape)

code.heading: train and Evaluate the Models
code.code:
# Train and evaluate Linear Regression
lr_pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)
lr_pred = lr_pipeline.predict(X_test)
lr_mse = mean_squared_error(y_test, lr_pred)
lr_r2 = r2_score(y_test, lr_pred)
lr_mae = mean_absolute_error(y_test, lr_pred)
lr_mape = mean_absolute_percentage_error(y_test, lr_pred)
lr_rmse = np.sqrt(lr_mse)

# Train and evaluate Ridge Regression
ridge_pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)
ridge_pred = ridge_pipeline.predict(X_test)
ridge_mse = mean_squared_error(y_test, ridge_pred)
ridhe_r2 = r2_score(y_test, ridge_pred)
ridge_mae = mean_absolute_error(y_test, ridge_pred)
ridge_mape = mean_absolute_percentage_error(y_test, ridge_pred)
ridge_rmse = np.sqrt(ridge_mse)

print("Linear Regression MSE:", lr_mse)
print("Ridge Regression MSE:", ridge_mse)

print("Linear Regression R2:", lr_r2)
print("Ridge Regression R2:", ridhe_r2)

print("Linear Regression MAE:", lr_mae)
print("Ridge Regression MAE:", ridge_mae)

print("Linear Regression MAPE:", lr_mape)
print("Ridge Regression MAPE:", ridge_mape)

print("Linear Regression RMSE:", lr_rmse)
print("Ridge Regression RMSE:", ridge_rmse)

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Absolute vs squared error trade-offs on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
